finding.claim: /checkout charges an amount computed entirely from client-supplied price and qty, with no server-side price lookup and no validation of sign, type, or finiteness.
finding.source: req.body.items[].price and req.body.items[].qty (JSON body, attacker-controlled). Precondition: logged-in user reaches the route (req.user set upstream).

trace.note: POST /checkout handler; no input schema or validation.
total = sum of i.price * i.qty, taken as-is from the body.
Attacker-chosen total passed directly to the charge call.
Total echoed back in the response.

finding.guards_checked: No server-side catalog price lookup (contrast /checkout-v2). No checks that price/qty are numbers, finite, non-negative, or that items is an array. No cap on total. Upstream auth sets req.user.id but nothing checks the amount. Unknown whether payments.charge rejects zero, negative, or non-finite amounts; must verify in payments module.

verdict.guard_found: none. cart.js:5 sums `i.price * i.qty` straight from req.body with no validation. cart.js:6 passes that total to req.payments.charge with no check on its result. The only other route, /checkout-v2 (cart.js:13-14), looks up prices server-side via req.catalog.price, but /checkout does not use it. The payments module is not in the directory, so I could not check whether charge rejects zero, negative, or non-finite amounts.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate: cart.js:4-7 takes the client-supplied price and qty (line 5) and charges that total (line 6) with no server-side price lookup. Even if payments.charge rejects negative or non-finite values, an attacker who is an ordinary logged-in user can still submit an arbitrary positive price (for example 0.01) and pay less than the catalog price, so no visible control blocks the attack.

finding.claim: /checkout-v2 can charge NaN: a missing or non-numeric qty propagates through Math.floor and Math.max, and an unknown SKU can propagate an undefined price.
finding.source: req.body.items[].qty omitted or non-numeric; or req.body.items[].sku unknown to catalog so catalog.price returns undefined.

trace.note: p = await req.catalog.price(i.sku); unknown SKU may yield undefined/NaN.
NaN total reaches the charge call.

finding.guards_checked: Math.max(1, ...) does not guard NaN. No Number.isFinite check on p, qty, or total. No SKU existence check. Catalog behaviour for unknown SKUs not visible here.

verdict.guard_found: none. cart.js:13-14 has no validation of p or i.qty, Math.max(1, Math.floor(i.qty)) at cart.js:14 returns NaN for undefined or non-numeric qty, and nothing between cart.js:14 and the charge call at cart.js:16 checks the total. No validation middleware is visible in this directory.
verdict.reason: At cart.js:14, a missing or non-numeric qty makes Math.floor(i.qty) NaN, Math.max(1, NaN) returns NaN, and total becomes NaN at cart.js:14, which is then passed unchecked to req.payments.charge at cart.js:16. The qty path is confirmed by code alone; the unknown-SKU path depends on catalog.price behaviour, which is not visible here, so it is unverified. The attacker is any caller of /checkout-v2 charging their own account, so impact is limited to a malformed charge or a failed charge, not privilege escalation, and the sink's handling of NaN is also not visible.

finding.claim: Attacker-controlled sku is passed to catalog.price with no type check, so an object-valued sku may cause injection if catalog builds queries from it.
finding.source: req.body.items[].sku (attacker-controlled; may be JSON object or array).
finding.sink: req.catalog.price(sku), cart.js:13 (catalog/DB query, not visible in this repo)

trace.note: for...of over req.body.items with no type checks.

finding.guards_checked: None in this file. Exploitability depends on catalog implementation (e.g. Mongo-style operators or SQL string building). Candidate only; needs verification in catalog module.

verdict.guard_found: none in cart.js. The only file in the directory is cart.js, so the catalog.price implementation (the sink) is not available to check. No type check, allowlist, or parameterization is visible at cart.js:12-13, and the route uses req.user.id (cart.js:16) but has no auth middleware in this file.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate: cart.js:12 iterates req.body.items and cart.js:13 passes the unvalidated i.sku to req.catalog.price, but whether an object-valued sku is exploitable depends on catalog.price, which is not in this repo, so the injection claim cannot be confirmed or refuted from the code available.

finding.claim: Neither checkout route is idempotent, so retries or double submissions double-charge the user.
finding.source: Repeated POST /checkout or /checkout-v2 (client retry, double-click, proxy retry).

trace.note: Each request calls charge with no idempotency key or order record.

finding.guards_checked: No idempotency key, order ID, or dedupe in this file. Whether payments.charge dedupes internally is unknown.

verdict.guard_found: none in cart.js: both routes pass req.user.id and a total straight to req.payments.charge at cart.js:6 and cart.js:16 with no idempotency key, order record, or dedupe. Grep for idempot|dedupe|orderId|order_id|charge found nothing beyond cart.js, so the payments implementation is not in the directory.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate (cart.js:6 and cart.js:16 each call req.payments.charge with no guard), but whether a repeated request double-charges depends on payments.charge, which is not in the available code, so the outcome cannot be decided here; and the only trigger named (double-click or proxy retry) is the user's own traffic, not an attacker gaining power, so this reads as a reliability defect rather than an exploitable vulnerability.

finding.claim: The v2 route has no cap on items or qty and performs sequential awaited catalog lookups, so a large request amplifies catalog load and latency.
finding.source: req.body.items with many entries, or very large qty values (e.g. 1e9).
finding.sink: Sequential req.catalog.price calls, cart.js:12-15; unbounded charge amount at cart.js:16

trace.note: One awaited catalog call per item, serially.
qty floored and max'd but not capped above.

finding.guards_checked: Math.max(1, Math.floor(qty)) sets a lower bound only. No max on items count, qty, or total. Any body-size limit lives in app setup, outside this file.

verdict.guard_found: None in cart.js. Math.max(1, Math.floor(i.qty)) at cart.js:14 is a lower bound only. No cap on items count, qty, or total at cart.js:12-16. The only directory file is cart.js, so app-level body-size limits (e.g. express body-parser's default ~100kb, if in use) cannot be checked here. Such a limit would bound item count indirectly, not per-item cost or qty.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches: cart.js:12 iterates req.body.items, cart.js:13 awaits one req.catalog.price per item serially, cart.js:14 floors and lower-bounds qty with no upper cap, and cart.js:16 charges the unbounded total. The route is reachable by any caller who gets past upstream auth (the handler reads req.user.id), so the amplification is real, though its severity is low and bounded by whatever body-size limit the app sets outside this file.
